clue.text: Dedicated traveller dismal after border setback

indicators.note: dismal's synonym comes after the turned border in the answer
a setback read as set back: the word for border is turned round

parts.note: a lip is the rim or border of a cup or crater
dismal means grim, gloomy

explanation.surface: A devoted traveller is glum after a hold-up at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a misfortune at the border, but it turns LIP into PIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person journeying devotedly to a shrine is a pilgrim: a near-synonym phrase.

clue.text: Expression shows the effects of strain on air

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: a rope or nerves fray under strain

explanation.surface: Someone's speech shows the stress of being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on air' looks like part of the strain; it signals a sound-alike. FRAYS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words, an expression or idiom.

clue.text: Ran through church in country

indicators.note: in places the church letters inside the country word

parts.note: land means a country
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted through a church in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' suggests running; it means pierced with a lance or blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce, so ran through means pierced, as with a sword.

clue.text: Agent worried about reduced hearing to return home

parts.note: a rep, a representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: about means the worried word goes around the shortened hearing

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

indicators.note: reduced means the last letter is cut

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A nervous agent, a little deaf, wants to go back to their own country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced hearing' looks like deafness, but it is a court hearing with its end cut, and 'about' wraps the worried word round it. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To repatriate is to return someone or oneself to their native country.

clue.text: Series of notes reflecting one problem with chapter

indicators.note: with places the chapter abbreviation alongside
reflecting means mirrored, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A sequence of notes thinks over a single problem with a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' reverses I SUM into MUSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Melody is a series of musical notes, a loose description of the art form.

clue.text: Old woman's predicament on following us

indicators.note: in this across entry the predicament word is placed on, i.e. after, the rest

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a spot is a tight corner or predicament

explanation.surface: An elderly woman complains about the trouble that follows us around.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Old woman stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old woman is an informal, slightly disparaging term for a fussy, timid person of either sex.

clue.text: Value our sailors in river like brothers

indicators.note: in places the value and sailors inside the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
rate means value, as in 'how do you rate it'
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's own sailors

explanation.surface: Our sailors in the river value each other like siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England; 'in' puts the other two pieces inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal derives from the Latin for brother, so it means brotherly.

clue.text: Keep back support

definitions.meaning: to hold back or check a flow, as of blood
the stalk supporting a leaf or flower, or the slender part holding a wine glass bowl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep back support' reads as a backrest; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to hold it back; a plant's main stalk supports its leaves and flowers.

clue.text: South American jockey in rave-up

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle, so the letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A South American rider at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like a rider; as a verb it shuffles the letters of 'in rave-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Peru is a South American.

clue.text: Salad items needed: cooked meats, too

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of 'meats, too' are prepared into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe says that salad items and cooked meats are needed too.
explanation.definitionFit: These red fruits are common components of a salad.

clue.text: Trip over in bowler's approach

parts.note: a run is a short trip, as in a run to the shops
up means over or finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler stumbles during the approach to the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip over' reads as stumbling; it is two separate pieces. In cricket the bowler runs towards the wicket before delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the bowler's approach to the crease before delivery is called the run-up.

clue.text: Killing man's heading off back — beat it!

indicators.note: back tells us to read the combined pieces from the end to the start

parts.note: killing means murder

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter, the head, of the word man's

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: After a killing, someone tells a man to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' sounds like 'go away', but it describes the instrument: something you beat. MURDER plus ANS (man's without its head M) is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument played by striking it with sticks, so it is a thing to beat.

clue.text: Marked beast, much loved, taken round Britain on display

indicators.note: the display word comes first and the rest sits on it, following it

parts.note: a spectacle is a striking public display or show

indicators.note: taken round says the loved word is wrapped around the letter for Britain

parts.note: dear means much loved
B is the abbreviation for Britain, as on international car plates

explanation.surface: A beloved animal is paraded around the country for people to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' wraps the much-loved word round the letter for Britain; 'on' puts the result after the display word.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American species has pale rings round its eyes, so it is a beast distinctively marked.

clue.text: Private sector's tax

indicators.note: a sector is a section, so the answer is a section of the word Private

explanation.surface: A question about the tax paid by the private sector of the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sector' looks like economic jargon; here it signals that a part of 'Private' is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Value added tax is the UK's sales tax, known by its abbreviation.

clue.text: Forecaster who goes round the houses?

definitions.text: Forecaster who goes round the houses?

parts.words: Forecaster who goes round the houses?
parts.note: suggests a door-to-door fortune teller, but the houses are the twelve divisions of the zodiac chart

explanation.surface: A predictor who talks in roundabout ways or calls door to door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round the houses' is British for being long-winded; here the houses are those of the horoscope.
explanation.definitionFit: One who predicts the future from planets moving through the twelve zodiac houses is a stargazing forecaster.

clue.text: Capital market's amount of business conducted before alleged scandal?

indicators.note: the business amount comes before the scandal word

parts.note: billings are the total amount of business a firm invoices in a period
-gate is the suffix tacked onto a name to label a supposed scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A London market's turnover comes ahead of rumours of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after market stands for 'is', a link; the question mark admits 'gate' is only a suffix.
explanation.definitionFit: This was London's famous wholesale fish market, so a market in the capital.

clue.text: Baron in story meeting magnanimously

indicators.note: in places the baron's letter inside the story

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A baron in a tale greets people with generous spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' gives LIE, a fib, not a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting generously and open-handedly is acting liberally, a close synonym.

clue.text: Scrambled last of eggs, highly seasoned

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word eggs

parts.note: curried means spiced with curry, highly seasoned

explanation.surface: The last scrambled eggs are heavily spiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' looks like the anagram signal or the eggs' cooking; it is the definition, meaning hurried.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to move hastily, so scrambled means hurried along.

clue.text: Elevated resilience, energy-packed, is inspiring

indicators.note: energy-packed means filled with the energy letter
elevated in a down clue means the word is read upward, i.e. reversed

parts.note: stamina is resilience, staying power
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Raised resilience, packed with energy, is uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reverses STAMINA to ANIMATS in this down entry; 'packed' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to give life or spirit to, so it is close to inspire.

clue.text: Force rodent outside small flat

indicators.note: outside says the rodent's letters go around the other two pieces

parts.note: a cony is a rabbit, an old word for the animal
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
tabular can mean flat and broad, like a tabletop

explanation.surface: Someone forces a rodent out of a small apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home; here it is an adjective meaning table-like. 'outside' wraps the rodent round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force, especially a regional British one.

clue.text: Previous drink knocked back amid cheers

indicators.note: amid places the reversed drink in the middle of the farewell word

parts.note: cheers is British slang for goodbye, i.e. bye

indicators.note: knocked back means reversed, though it suggests gulping a drink

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink to cheers before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses NOG to GON. 'cheers' is British for thanks or goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygone means past or former, a synonym of previous.

clue.text: Expert locks up old books without delay

indicators.note: locks up means confines, so the expert holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A specialist secures old books right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old books' looks like the Old Testament; it is the letter for old plus the New Testament, which 'locks up' sets inside the expert word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto, from Spanish and Italian, is informal for immediately.

clue.text: Female animal almost turned into a male

indicators.note: turned means the shortened word is reversed
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A female animal is turned into a male, as if by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MARE to MAR and 'turned' reverses that; 'into a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is an uncastrated male sheep, an example of a male animal.

clue.text: Construction worker's course?

parts.note: sounds like a builder's training course, but a course is also a row of bricks in a wall, laid by this tradesman

explanation.surface: What training does a building-site worker take?
explanation.walkthrough: A course in bricklaying is a horizontal row of bricks; the worker who lays them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman lays courses of bricks, so a course is his work; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Copper coin couple found in yard, perhaps, long ago

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Copper coins are dug up together in a back yard from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' means join the two pieces. A threepenny bit was an old British coin. The yard is a measure of length, not a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient unit of length like the yard, based on the forearm, so an old measure.

clue.text: See 11
Being a member, where one expects to be?

definitions.meaning: belonging to a society or association
British slang for pregnant, i.e. expecting a baby

explanation.walkthrough: 'expects' means 'is expecting a baby'; the phrase is British slang for being pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a club member is inside the club; in British slang the phrase also means pregnant.

clue.text: Raised bank within garden's borders

indicators.note: within means the bank word sits inside the border letters
borders means only the outermost letters of garden are used

parts.note: a row, as in a bank of seats or oars, is a tier

explanation.surface: A raised bank sits within the edges of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' looks like flower beds; it picks the outside letters G and N of 'garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised as in bred or cultivated: plants or children that have been raised are grown.

clue.text: Screen man who rides again bearing old dispatch

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the cowboy's name holds the letter for old

parts.note: Destry Rides Again is a 1939 Hollywood Western; its hero is the screen cowboy

explanation.surface: A film cowboy comes back with an old message to send.
explanation.walkthrough: Destry Rides Again is a 1939 Western starring James Stewart; O goes inside DESTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch is to kill or finish off, a synonym of wiping out.

clue.text: Missile destroyed depot storing gold

indicators.note: storing means the rearranged letters keep the gold symbol inside them
destroyed means the word depot is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A missile hit a depot where gold was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the depot letters to TPEDO, and 'storing' holds the heraldic gold inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon fired from a ship or submarine is a kind of missile.
